{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-wi-d","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"f18b511c056b463db4da603bb48ac6bd6ae9b2240e42f1c08d135d3864fa699c","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-wi-class-d:lineage:1","source_registry_sha256":"9dcfc0d0c3044debd01d4cb03103f48fb860797364a23b2cb56d36c868619a64","source_liveness_sha256":"4ca51030ff51b3372629ada1c05ad91f501dabccdcf7931dab678c717e7bb9b6"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C2"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C2","chunk_id":"C2.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Driving test confusables: signs test versus knowledge test, vision rules and road test logistics","heading":"C2 — Confusable pairs and knowledge-graph hints: the two written tests, the two vision standards and walk-in versus appointment testing","learner_facing":false,"markdown":"## C2 — Confusable pairs and knowledge-graph hints: the two written tests, the two vision standards and walk-in versus appointment testing
Confusable pairs among the four Wisconsin driving tests, followed by continuation facts on vision referrals and road test preparation; each block ties to one handbook page, and hint metadata sits only in the trailing line of a block.

FACT_ID: sec01-R01 | anchor: A01
Both written tests use the same 80 percent bar, but the highway signs test is 12 right out of 15 while the knowledge test is 40 right out of 50. [A01]
Why it matters: group written tests; confusable signs test versus knowledge test question counts.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-R02 | anchor: A01
The highway signs test is about reading signs that regulate, warn and direct traffic, while the knowledge test is about traffic laws. [A01]
Why it matters: group written tests; confusable test content.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-R03 | anchor: A01
The acuity rule of at least 20/40 needs to be met in only one eye, but the 70-degree field-of-vision rule is measured from the center of each eye. [A01]
Why it matters: group vision; confusable one eye versus each eye.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-R04 | anchor: A01
The 20/40 acuity standard may be met with or without corrective lenses, so wearing glasses does not by itself fail the screening. [A01]
Why it matters: group vision; difficulty low.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-R05 | anchor: A01
The DMV can run the vision screening itself, but after a failed screening the applicant goes to a vision specialist carrying form MV3030V/T579. [A01]
Why it matters: group vision; confusable DMV screening versus specialist exam.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-R06 | anchor: A01
The signs and knowledge tests are free at a DMV customer service center, while the online knowledge test option for ages 15 to 17 costs $10. [A01]
Why it matters: group written tests; confusable free in person versus paid online.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-R07 | anchor: A01
The handbook mentions the online knowledge test option only for applicants between ages 15 and 17, and that option carries a fee. [A01]
Why it matters: group written tests; difficulty medium.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-R08 | anchor: A01
Because the knowledge test takes about 45 minutes, the handbook says to start early enough to finish before the customer service center closes. [A01]
Why it matters: group written tests; misconception late arrival.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-R09 | anchor: A02
The two written tests are walk-in, but the skills test is appointment-only and is scheduled on the DMV road test web page. [A02]
Why it matters: group logistics; confusable walk-in versus appointment.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-R10 | anchor: A02
The road test, the driving test and the skills test are three names for the same on-road exam with a DMV examiner. [A02]
Why it matters: group skills test; confusable names.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-R11 | anchor: A02
The examiner checks the car before any driving starts, looking at the horn, lights and signals, plates, doors and mirrors to make sure it is safe to drive. [A02]
Why it matters: group skills test; misconception driver only is graded.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-R12 | anchor: A02
Knowing where the headlight, wiper and defrost controls are is part of being ready for the road test, not an optional extra. [A02]
Why it matters: group skills test; difficulty low.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-R13 | anchor: A02
Intersections are graded both ways on the road test: the ones where you must stop and the ones you approach without a stop. [A02]
Why it matters: group skills test; confusable stop versus no-stop intersections.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-R14 | anchor: A02
A Y-turn appears both as an example examiner instruction and as one of the listed maneuvers, alongside the roadside stop and start and parking. [A02]
Why it matters: group skills test; difficulty medium.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0006]
